title: AI Root Cause Analysis Shifts from Model Reasoning to Context Engineering
gist: Observability vendor Coroot's engineer Nikolay Sivko separated AI root cause analysis into two measurable jobs — the model's reasoning and the harness that decides what data reaches it — and tested a single deliberately misleading ~9,800-token context against eleven models. Claude Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro all passed; among self-hostable models only Gemma 4 31B identified the root cause while the larger Qwen3.6 35B and Qwen3 Coder Next missed it. Sivko's conclusion, echoed by Dynatrace's deterministic Davis AI and by practitioners abandoning fully agentic designs, is that reasoning is basically solved and the harness is now the hard part.

themes.theme: Reframing AI RCA: harness vs model

insights.claim: A growing view among observability engineers holds that LLM reasoning ability is no longer the bottleneck in AI-assisted root cause analysis, and that the harder problem now sits in the pipeline deciding what data reaches the model.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: If reasoning is commoditised, the defensible value in AIOps sits in the data pipeline, not in model access — a repricing signal for observability vendors versus model vendors.
insights.quote: the reasoning ability of large language models is no longer the bottleneck in AI-assisted root cause analysis, and that the harder problem now sits in the pipeline that decides what data reaches the model

insights.claim: Coroot engineer Nikolay Sivko splits AI RCA into two separately measurable jobs — reasoning over the data in front of the model, and the harness deciding what data reaches it in what shape — and argues that 'can AI do RCA?' is therefore the wrong question.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: A benchmarking discipline for anyone evaluating AIOps claims: demand harness-held-constant model comparisons, otherwise the number measures nothing.
insights.quote: He argued that "can AI do RCA?" is the wrong question, because the two jobs need to be measured apart.

insights.claim: Coroot's pipeline correlates signals into findings and passes them to the model in a single focused context with no agent loop, a design choice whose specific evaluation benefit is that a wrong answer can be blamed on the model rather than on missing evidence.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Deterministic harnesses buy attributability, which is a prerequisite for improving a system at all — the underrated argument against agent loops.
insights.quote: Coroot's pipeline correlates signals into findings and passes them to the model in one focused context with no agent loop, which lets a wrong answer be blamed on the model rather than on missing evidence.

insights.claim: Because agent-based and deterministic RCA designs break in different ways, a failed diagnosis in an agentic system cannot be attributed between weak reasoning and a harness that fed the model the wrong evidence.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Unattributable failures make iterative improvement impossible — a structural reason agentic incident-response products stall after the demo.
insights.quote: The two approaches break in different ways, which makes it hard to tell whether a failed diagnosis came from weak reasoning or from a harness that fed the model the wrong evidence.
insights.locator: 'Most AI RCA efforts fall into two camps'

insights.claim: Dynatrace's Davis AI independently exemplifies the deterministic camp, using topology-based causal analysis that traverses a real-time dependency map to pinpoint a root cause rather than turning an LLM loose in an open-ended agent loop.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Two independent observability vendors converging on deterministic correlation is evidence of an industry-level architectural shift, not a single vendor's preference.
insights.quote: Dynatrace's Davis AI likewise leans on deterministic, topology-based causal analysis, traversing a real-time dependency map to pinpoint a root cause rather than turning an LLM loose in an open-ended agent loop.
insights.locator: 'Most AI RCA efforts fall into two camps'

insights.claim: Sivko's test scenario was a Chaos Mesh NetworkChaos experiment injecting delay between a catalogue service and its Postgres database, slowing queries and pushing the front-end into 502 errors, with the same ~9,800-token prompt run against eleven models asking for root cause, cause-and-effect chain and immediate fix.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: A ~9,800-token single-shot context is the whole input — a reference point for how compact a well-engineered RCA context can be versus multi-turn agent transcripts.
insights.quote: He then ran the same prompt, around 9,800 tokens, against eleven models, asking each for the root cause, the cause-and-effect chain, and the immediate fix.
insights.locator: 'To test it, Sivko built one scenario'

insights.claim: The evaluation context was deliberately seeded with misleading signals, including query timings inflated by network round-trip time, so passing required a model to reject a plausible database-slowness explanation in favour of the injected network delay.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Adversarial context design is how RCA evals avoid rewarding pattern-matching — copy this test construction when evaluating AIOps vendors.
insights.quote: The context deliberately included misleading signals, including query timings inflated by network round-trip time.
insights.locator: 'To test it, Sivko built one scenario'

insights.claim: Closed frontier models Claude Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro all passed the RCA test, naming the chaos experiment as the cause and flagging the need to delete both the experiment and its schedule — a complete remediation, not just a diagnosis.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Frontier-model parity on this task means model choice is not a differentiator at the top of the market — competition moves to price and to the surrounding pipeline.
insights.quote: Closed frontier models Claude Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro all passed, naming the experiment and flagging the need to delete both it and its schedule.

insights.claim: Among self-hostable models the results inverted expected scaling: Gemma 4 31B was the only one to identify the root cause, while the larger Qwen3.6 35B and Qwen3 Coder Next both missed it.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Parameter count fails as a proxy for RCA capability in the self-hosted tier — teams with data-residency constraints must test on their own harness rather than pick by size.
insights.quote: Gemma 4 31B was the only self-hostable model to identify the root cause, while the larger Qwen3.6 35B and Qwen3 Coder Next both missed it.

insights.claim: Larger open-weight models mostly kept pace with the closed frontier models on the RCA task, narrowing the practical gap for teams that cannot send telemetry to a hosted API.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Open-weight viability on a real operational task erodes the pricing power of hosted frontier APIs in regulated observability deployments.
insights.quote: Larger open-weight models mostly kept pace.

themes.theme: Where agentic designs still win, and why teams abandon them anyway

insights.claim: Agent-based RCA retains a genuine advantage that deterministic pipelines cannot replicate: a model fetching its own data can pull signals a fixed correlation set never anticipated, which matters specifically for novel incidents.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: The deterministic shift caps coverage at the known-incident set — the residual novel-incident tail is where agentic tooling keeps a market.
insights.quote: since a model that fetches its own data can pull signals a fixed pipeline never anticipated, which matters for novel incidents outside a predefined correlation set
insights.locator: 'The findings do not settle the debate'

insights.claim: Accounts from ZenML and Incident.io describe multi-agent LLM investigations as notoriously hard to debug in production because a failed run leaves no clean stack trace, only unpredictable prompt interactions and emergent coordination between agents.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Undebuggability is the operational cost that shows up after deployment, not during evaluation — the gap between agentic demo success and production abandonment.
insights.quote: because a failed run leaves no clean stack trace, only unpredictable prompt interactions and emergent coordination between agents
insights.locator: 'They pay for that flexibility in operability'

insights.claim: Engineers discussing the trade-off on Reddit report scrapping fully agentic designs in favour of mostly deterministic workflows with a single narrow LLM step, citing both better reliability and lower token cost.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Practitioner behaviour, not vendor marketing, is moving toward narrow-LLM architectures — a demand-side signal against fully autonomous agent products.
insights.quote: engineers discussing the trade-off on Reddit report scrapping fully agentic designs in favour of mostly deterministic workflows with a narrow LLM step, citing better reliability and lower token cost
insights.locator: 'That fragility pushes many practitioners the other way'

themes.theme: Cost economics and where the next engineering effort goes

insights.claim: Sivko notes that a single short RCA call runs a few cents even on frontier models, specifically because the correlation work happens before the model is called rather than inside an agent loop.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Front-loading correlation collapses per-incident inference cost to cents, which removes token price as an objection to AI-assisted incident response entirely.
insights.quote: a single short call runs a few cents even on frontier models, because the correlation work happens before the model is called

insights.claim: Sivko judges the reasoning component of AI RCA to be basically solved and states the real remaining work is preparing the right, compact context for the model before calling it, redirecting engineering effort from model selection to harness design.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Budget allocation follows: spend on telemetry correlation and context assembly, not on upgrading to a larger model.
insights.quote: the real work is now "preparing the right, compact context for the model before you call it"
insights.locator: 'He judged that the reasoning part of AI RCA'

insights.claim: Guidance from Anthropic, LangChain and observability vendor Mezmo converges on the same principle — curating the smallest set of high-signal, compact context is now a core discipline for reliable LLM reasoning — making context engineering a cross-vendor consensus rather than one team's finding.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Context engineering is consolidating as a named discipline with vendor-published doctrine — an emerging skills category and tooling market to size.
insights.quote: curating the smallest set of high-signal, compact context is now a core discipline for making LLM-based reasoning and observability reliable
insights.locator: 'That framing echoes a wider push around context engineering'
